subject: A Level Physics
title: Electron in a magnetic field
question:
Fig. 3.1 shows the path of an electron that enters a region of uniform magnetic field directed into the page. The electron moves in a semicircle of radius r and leaves the field.
(a) Explain why the path of the electron in the field is circular.
(b) Show that r = mv / Be.
(c) State and explain the effect on the path of doubling the speed v.

scene: The electron curves downwards, which is the correct direction for a negative charge with the field into the page.
The crosses that would sit on the path are left out so the path stays clear.
tikz: First try: a leftover line in the code drew an extra arrow from the centre.

figure:
A region of uniform magnetic field into the page, shown as a dashed rectangle filled with a regular grid of × marks.
An electron travelling at speed v moves to the right, along a straight line, into the field at the left edge.
Inside the field, it follows a semicircle that curves downwards, which is correct for a negative charge, and leaves the field moving to the left along a line below where it entered.
The centre of the semicircle is on the left edge of the field. Mark it with a dot and draw the radius r from it to the path.
Show arrows on the straight parts of the path. No × mark should sit on the path.
Label: electron, speed v, and the radius r. Title above the field: uniform magnetic field into the page.
